name: NewtonIntegrator
description: Integrate acceleration to velocity and velocity to position using Newton's second law. Handles both translational and rotational motion. Most common integrator in YADE simulations.

attributes.name: damping
attributes.description: Non-viscous damping coefficient (0-1). Applies numerical damping to accelerations to help reach quasi-static equilibrium faster. 0 = no damping, typically 0.2-0.4.

attributes.name: gravity
attributes.description: Gravitational acceleration applied to all dynamic bodies. Example: (0, 0, -9.81) for Earth gravity.

attributes.name: maxVelocitySq
attributes.description: stores max. displacement, based on which we trigger collision detection. (auto-updated)

attributes.name: exactAsphericalRot
attributes.description: Use exact aspherical body rotation integration. More accurate for non-spherical bodies (clumps).

attributes.name: prevVelGrad
attributes.description: Store previous velocity gradient (velGrad) to track average acceleration in periodic simulations. (auto-updated)

attributes.name: warnNoForceReset
attributes.description: Warn when forces were not resetted in this step by ForceResetter; this mostly points to ForceResetter being forgotten incidentally and should be disabled only with a good reason.

attributes.name: kinSplit
attributes.description: Whether to separately track translational and rotational kinetic energy.

attributes.name: dampGravity
attributes.description: By default, numerical damping applies to ALL forces, even gravity. If this option is set to false, then the gravity forces calculated based on NewtonIntegrator.gravity are excluded from the damping calculation. This option has no effect on gravity forces added by GravityEngine.

attributes.name: mask
attributes.description: If mask defined and the bitwise AND between mask and body`s groupMask gives 0, the body will not move/rotate. Velocities and accelerations will be calculated not paying attention to this parameter.

attributes.name: densityScaling
attributes.description: if True, then density scaling [Pfc3dManual30]_ will be applied in order to have a critical timestep equal to targetDt for all bodies. This option makes the simulation unrealistic from a dynamic point of view, but may speedup quasistatic simulations. In rare situations, it could be useful to not set the scalling factor automatically for each body (which the time-stepper does). In such case revert GlobalStiffnessTimeStepper.densityScaling to False.

attributes.name: dead
attributes.description: If true, this engine will not run at all; can be used for making an engine temporarily deactivated and only resurrect it at a later point.

attributes.name: ompThreads
attributes.description: Number of threads to be used in the engine. If ompThreads<0 (default), the number will be typically OMP_NUM_THREADS or the number N defined by 'yade -jN' (this behavior can depend on the engine though). This attribute will only affect engines whose code includes openMP parallel regions (e.g. InteractionLoop). This attribute is mostly useful for experiments or when combining ParallelEngine with engines that run parallel regions, resulting in nested OMP loops with different number of threads at each level.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Textual label for this object; must be valid python identifier, you can refer to it directly from python.

attributes.name: execTime
attributes.description: Cumulative time in nanoseconds this Engine took to run (only used if O.timingEnabled == ``True``).

attributes.name: execCount
attributes.description: Cumulative count this engine was run (only used if O.timingEnabled == ``True``).

attributes.name: timingDeltas
attributes.description: Detailed information about timing inside the Engine itself. Empty unless enabled in the source code and O.timingEnabled == ``True``.
